query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a chromium-rich coating to refractory high-entropy alloys can improve their high-temperature oxygen resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloy in its as-cast or homogenized state
generation.intervention: Deposition of a chromium-rich coating via electro spark deposition or similar method
generation.conditions: Exposure to high-temperature oxygen-rich environments, such as those found in geothermal or aerospace applications, at temperatures between 500°C to 1000°C
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a passivation layer containing chromium oxide on the surface of the coating
generation.mechanism: The chromium-rich coating forms a protective layer that reduces the corrosion current density and prevents oxygen diffusion into the underlying alloy, thereby improving its high-temperature oxygen resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature oxygen resistance, as measured by a reduction in corrosion rate or oxidation kinetics, compared to the uncoated alloy
generation.baseline: The corrosion rate or oxidation kinetics of the uncoated refractory high-entropy alloy under the same conditions
generation.boundary: The temperature range (500°C to 1000°C) and atmosphere (oxygen-rich) under which the coating is effective
generation.uncertainty: The long-term stability and adhesion of the coating, as well as the potential for chromium depletion or degradation over time

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the high-temperature oxygen resistance of coated and uncoated refractory high-entropy alloys in a controlled environment
measurements: Microstructural analysis of the coating and underlying alloy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated alloy shows no significant improvement in high-temperature oxygen resistance compared to the uncoated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: Can CoCrFeNiMo0.85 high-entropy alloy coatings, produced via mechanical alloying and electro spark deposition, provide effective corrosion resistance and adhesion for stainless steel substrates in aggressive geothermal environments?. System: CoCrFeNiMo0.85 high-entropy alloy deposited on 316 L stainless steel substrate. Processing: Solid-state processing: Mechanical alloying of high-purity Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, Mo powders for 30 h in a Pulverisette 6 Classic Line planetary ball mill (350 RPM, ball-to-powder ratio 10:1, N-Heptane process control agent) under Argon; cold pressing at 250 kN into 25 mm × 5 mm samples; sintering at 1100 °C for 1 h; machining into electrodes; electro spark deposition (ESD) under Argon atmosphere to deposit successive layers.. Test conditions: Pull-off testing per ASTM D4541–01; electrochemical corrosion testing in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at 25 ± 0.5 °C for 6 h using potentiodynamic polarization..
